rules.statement: Interval changes. Flexible mode: monthly to yearly prorates the yearly price over the remaining time and keeps the anchor; yearly to monthly keeps the anchor while the proration date is inside the new monthly period and is rejected past it. Classic mode: an interval change resets the billing cycle to the clock time. Yearly to yearly keeps the period. In flexible mode each item keeps its own billing period; a proration date exactly at the new period end is accepted. Classic mode refuses mixed intervals, and flexible mixed intervals refuse a forever amount-off coupon.

rules.statement: A percent-off coupon takes round(percent × sum) from the discountable lines it applies to and spreads it across them by a running rounded-down total: each line gets floor(running share) minus what earlier lines already got. This includes the first invoice, whose allocation sets the discount a flexible credit carries (wide3-256 for four lines).

rules.statement: Classic mode: proration lines are not discountable. The credit is -round_half_away(net × r/P), where net is the old item's amount after applying, in subscription order and to that item alone, every discount on the subscription when the credited period was billed: an amount-off in full, a percent-off as round(pct × what is left), never below 0. The share each discount got on the billing invoice is irrelevant, a share of 0 included. The charge prorates first and subtracts the prorated discount after.

provenance.ref: spent batch 3, analysed in analysis/hold-b3-failures.md (2026-10-13), and dev fixtures

rules.statement: A once coupon is used up only by an invoice where it actually took something off; a subscription's once coupon that took nothing stays active (dev-brk-free-once, wide3-027, -054, -230, -249). A once coupon passed to the preview discounts the remaining-time charge and is then used up, so it no longer discounts the renewal; when the change prorates nothing it discounts the renewal and is listed; in an immediate invoice it is listed at 0. A remaining-time charge uses a once coupon up as soon as its full-period share is above 0, even when the prorated share rounds to 0 (dev-v5-dsc-013, dev-v5-dsc-052).

rules.statement: Flexible mode, immediate invoice: proration lines list their discounts at 0. The credit line lists nothing when the invoice has no discount. It lists the invoice's discounts when the billed line carried none. It lists nothing when no carried discount survives DSC-08. Otherwise it lists the surviving carried discounts still on the invoice, in subscription order. If there are none, it lists the invoice's discounts when a carried discount is still on the invoice, else, when the billed line carried a single discount, that discount (a spent once coupon, or one replaced by a coupon passed to the preview), else the invoice's discounts. A carried discount that took 0 counts only while it is still on the invoice. A non-immediate flexible preview lists the invoice's first discount, a dropped one included.
